data.captureNote: OTP 2.9 GTFS GraphQL introspection for plan selection used in recorded/*.json a–c. Aliases: startTime←start, endTime←end.

fields.name: date
fields.description: The time and date of travel. Format: Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

fields.name: debugOutput
fields.description: Information about the timings for the plan generation

fields.name: from
fields.description: The origin

fields.name: itineraries
fields.description: A list of possible itineraries

fields.name: messageEnums
fields.description: A list of possible error messages as enum

fields.name: messageStrings
fields.description: A list of possible error messages in cleartext

fields.name: nextPageCursor
fields.description:
Use the cursor to go to the next "page" of itineraries. Copy the cursor from the last response
to the pageCursor query parameter and keep the original request as is. This will enable you to
search for itineraries in the next search-window.
The cursor based paging only support stepping to the next page, as it does not support jumping.
This is only usable when public transportation mode(s) are included in the query.

fields.name: previousPageCursor
fields.description:
Use the cursor to go to the previous "page" of itineraries. Copy the cursor from the last
response to the pageCursor query parameter and keep the original request otherwise as is.
This will enable you to search for itineraries in the previous search-window.
The cursor based paging only support stepping to the previous page, as it does not support
jumping.
This is only usable when public transportation mode(s) are included in the query.

fields.name: routingErrors
fields.description: A list of routing errors, and fields which caused them

fields.name: to
fields.description: The destination

fields.name: accessibilityScore
fields.description:
Computes a numeric accessibility score between 0 and 1.
  
The closer the value is to 1 the better the wheelchair-accessibility of this itinerary is.
A value of `null` means that no score has been computed, not that the leg is inaccessible.
  
More information is available in the [feature documentation](https://docs.opentripplanner.org/en/dev-2.x/sandbox/IBIAccessibilityScore/).

fields.name: arrivedAtDestinationWithRentedBicycle
fields.description: Does the itinerary end without dropping off the rented bicycle:

fields.name: duration
fields.description: Duration of the trip on this itinerary, in seconds.

fields.name: elevationGained
fields.description: How much elevation is gained, in total, over the course of the itinerary, in meters.

fields.name: elevationLost
fields.description: How much elevation is lost, in total, over the course of the itinerary, in meters.

fields.name: emissionsPerPerson
fields.description: Emissions of this itinerary per traveler.

fields.name: end
fields.description: Time when the user leaves arrives at the destination.

fields.name: generalizedCost
fields.description: Generalized cost of the itinerary. Used for debugging search results.

fields.name: legs
fields.description:
A list of Legs. Each Leg is either a walking (cycling, car) portion of the
itinerary, or a transit leg on a particular vehicle. So a itinerary where the
user walks to the Q train, transfers to the 6, then walks to their
destination, has four legs.

fields.name: numberOfTransfers
fields.description:
How many transfers are part of this itinerary.
  
Notes:
 - Interlined/stay-seated transfers do not increase this count.
 - Transferring from a flex to a fixed schedule trip and vice versa increases this count.

fields.name: start
fields.description: Time when the user leaves from the origin.

fields.name: systemNotices
fields.description:
A list of system notices. Contains debug information for itineraries.
One use-case is to run a routing search with 'debugItineraryFilter: true'.
This will then tag itineraries instead of removing them from the result.
This make it possible to inspect the itinerary-filter-chain.

fields.name: waitingTime
fields.description: How much time is spent waiting for transit to arrive, in seconds.

fields.name: walkDistance
fields.description: How far the user has to walk, in meters.

fields.name: walkTime
fields.description: How much time is spent walking, in seconds.

fields.name: accessibilityScore
fields.description:
Computes a numeric accessibility score between 0 and 1.
  
The closer the value is to 1 the better the wheelchair-accessibility of this leg is.
A value of `null` means that no score has been computed, not that the itinerary is inaccessible.
  
More information is available in the [feature documentation](https://docs.opentripplanner.org/en/dev-2.x/sandbox/IBIAccessibilityScore/).

fields.name: agency
fields.description: For transit legs, the transit agency that operates the service used for this leg. For non-transit legs, `null`.

fields.name: alerts
fields.description: Applicable alerts for this leg.

fields.name: distance
fields.description: The distance traveled while traversing the leg in meters.

fields.name: dropOffBookingInfo
fields.description:
Special booking information for the drop off stop of this leg if, for example, it needs
to be booked in advance. This could be due to a flexible or on-demand service.

fields.name: dropoffType
fields.description: This is used to indicate if alighting from this leg is possible only with special arrangements.

fields.name: duration
fields.description: The leg's duration in seconds

fields.name: end
fields.description: The time when the leg ends including real-time information, if available.

fields.name: fareProducts
fields.description:
Fare products are purchasable tickets which may have an optional fare container or rider
category that limits who can buy them or how.
  
Please read the documentation of `id` very carefully to learn how a single fare product
that applies to multiple legs can appear several times.

fields.name: from
fields.description: The Place where the leg originates.

fields.name: generalizedCost
fields.description: Generalized cost of the leg. Used for debugging search results.

fields.name: headsign
fields.description:
For transit legs, the headsign that the vehicle shows at the stop where the passenger boards.
For non-transit legs, null.

fields.name: id
fields.description:
An identifier for the leg, which can be used to re-fetch transit leg information, except leg's fare products.
Re-fetching fails when the underlying transit data no longer exists.
**Note:** when both id and fare products are queried with [Relay](https://relay.dev/), id should be queried using a suitable GraphQL alias
such as `legId: id`. Relay does not accept different fare product ids in otherwise identical legs.
  
The identifier is valid for a maximum of 2 years, but sometimes it will fail after a few hours.
We do not recommend storing IDs for a long time.

fields.name: interlineWithPreviousLeg
fields.description:
Interlines with previous leg.
This is true when the same vehicle is used for the previous leg as for this leg
and passenger can stay inside the vehicle.

fields.name: legGeometry
fields.description: The leg's geometry.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: The mode (e.g. `WALK`) used when traversing this leg.

fields.name: nextLegs
fields.description: Future legs with same origin and destination stops or stations

fields.name: pickupBookingInfo
fields.description:
Special booking information for the pick up stop of this leg if, for example, it needs
to be booked in advance. This could be due to a flexible or on-demand service.

fields.name: pickupType
fields.description: This is used to indicate if boarding this leg is possible only with special arrangements.

fields.name: previousLegs
fields.description: Previous legs with same origin and destination stops or stations

fields.name: realTime
fields.description: Whether there is real-time data about this Leg

fields.name: realtimeState
fields.description: State of real-time data

fields.name: rentedBike
fields.description: Whether this leg is traversed with a rented vehicle.

fields.name: rideHailingEstimate
fields.description: Estimate of a hailed ride like Uber.

fields.name: route
fields.description: For transit legs, the route that is used for traversing the leg. For non-transit legs, `null`.

fields.name: serviceDate
fields.description: For transit legs, the service date of the trip. Format: YYYYMMDD. For non-transit legs, null.

fields.name: start
fields.description: The time when the leg starts including real-time information, if available.

fields.name: steps
fields.description: The turn-by-turn navigation instructions.

fields.name: stopCalls
fields.description:
All the stop calls (stop times) of this _leg_ (but not trip) including the boarding and alighting one.
  
Non-transit legs return an empty list.

fields.name: to
fields.description: The Place where the leg ends.

fields.name: transitLeg
fields.description: Whether this leg is a transit leg or not.

fields.name: trip
fields.description: For transit legs, the trip that is used for traversing the leg. For non-transit legs, `null`.

fields.name: walkingBike
fields.description: Whether this leg is walking with a bike.

fields.name: arrival
fields.description:
The time the rider will arrive at the place. This also includes real-time information
if available.

fields.name: departure
fields.description:
The time the rider will depart the place. This also includes real-time information
if available.

fields.name: lat
fields.description: Latitude of the place (WGS 84)

fields.name: lon
fields.description: Longitude of the place (WGS 84)

fields.name: name
fields.description: For transit stops, the name of the stop. For points of interest, the name of the POI.

fields.name: rentalVehicle
fields.description: The rental vehicle related to the place

fields.name: stop
fields.description: The stop related to the place.

fields.name: stopPosition
fields.description:
The position of the stop in the pattern. This is not required to start from 0 or be consecutive - any
increasing integer sequence along the stops is valid.
  
The purpose of this field is to identify the stop within the pattern so it can be cross-referenced
between it and the itinerary. It is safe to cross-reference when done quickly, i.e. within seconds.
However, it should be noted that real-time updates can change the values, so don't store it for
longer amounts of time.
  
Depending on the source data, this might not be the GTFS `stop_sequence` but another value, perhaps
even generated.
  
The position can be either at a certain stop or in between two for trips where this is possible.

fields.name: vehicleParking
fields.description: The vehicle parking related to the place

fields.name: vehicleRentalStation
fields.description: The vehicle rental station related to the place

fields.name: viaLocationType
fields.description:
This defines if the place is a requested via location, and what kind it is. If the value is
`null`, this place is not a via location.

Route.name: Route
Route.description:
Route represents a public transportation service, usually from point A to point
B and *back*, shown to customers under a single name, e.g. bus 550. Routes
contain patterns (see field `patterns`), which describe different variants of
the route, e.g. outbound pattern from point A to point B and inbound pattern
from point B to point A.

fields.name: agency
fields.description: Agency operating the route

fields.name: alerts
fields.description:
List of alerts which have an effect on the route directly or indirectly.
By default only alerts directly affecting this route are returned. It's also possible
to return other relevant alerts through defining types.

fields.name: color
fields.description:
The color (in hexadecimal format) the agency operating this route would prefer
to use on UI elements (e.g. polylines on a map) related to this route. This
value is not available for most routes.

fields.name: gtfsId
fields.description: ID of the route in format `FeedId:RouteId`

fields.name: id
fields.description: Global object ID provided by Relay. This value can be used to refetch this object using **node** query.

fields.name: isReplacement
fields.description:
Is this a replacement route.
Only true for GTFS-sourced data if set by the extended GTFS route type, because GTFS does not implement
replacement links, so replacement trips in GTFS cannot mechanically state their original trip.
In NeTEx/SIRI-sourced data this can be set by either a replacement submode, or a replacement
link in a DatedServiceJourney.

fields.name: longName
fields.description: Long name of the route, e.g. Helsinki-Leppävaara

fields.name: mode
fields.description: Transport mode of this route, e.g. `BUS`

fields.name: patterns
fields.description: List of patterns which operate on this route

fields.name: replacementsExist
fields.description:
Do any trips of this route have any linked replacements.
Only ever true with NeTEx or SIRI, because GTFS does not implement replacement
links, so replacement trips in GTFS cannot mechanically state their original trip.

fields.name: shortName
fields.description: Short name of the route, usually a line number, e.g. 550

fields.name: sortOrder
fields.description:
Orders the routes in a way which is useful for presentation to passengers.
Routes with smaller values should be displayed first.
  
The value can be any non-negative integer. A null value means that no information was supplied.
  
This value is passed through from the source data without modification. If multiple feeds
define sort orders for their routes, they may not be comparable to each other as no agreed scale
exists.
  
Two routes may also have the same sort order and clients must decide based on other criteria
what the actual order is.

fields.name: stops
fields.description: List of stops on this route

fields.name: textColor
fields.description:
The color (in hexadecimal format) the agency operating this route would prefer
to use when displaying text related to this route. This value is not available
for most routes.

fields.name: trips
fields.description: List of trips which operate on this route

fields.name: type
fields.description:
The raw GTFS route type as a integer. For the list of possible values, see:
https://developers.google.com/transit/gtfs/reference/#routestxt and
https://developers.google.com/transit/gtfs/reference/extended-route-types

Stop.name: Stop
Stop.description:
Stop can represent either a single public transport stop, where passengers can
board and/or disembark vehicles, or a station, which contains multiple stops.
See field `locationType`.

fields.name: alerts
fields.description:
By default, list of alerts which have directly an effect on just the stop.
It's also possible to return other relevant alerts through defining types.

fields.name: code
fields.description: Stop code which is visible at the stop

fields.name: desc
fields.description: Description of the stop, usually a street name

fields.name: geometries
fields.description:
Representations of this stop's geometry. This is mainly interesting for flex stops which can be
a polygon or a group of stops either consisting of either points or polygons.
  
Regular fixed-schedule stops return a single point.
  
Stations (parent stations with child stops) contain a geometry collection with a point for the
central coordinate plus a convex hull polygon (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convex_hull) of all
coordinates of the child stops.
  
If there are only two child stops then the convex hull is a straight line between the them. If
there is a single child stop then it's a single point.

fields.name: gtfsId
fields.description: ÌD of the stop in format `FeedId:StopId`

fields.name: id
fields.description: Global object ID provided by Relay. This value can be used to refetch this object using **node** query.

fields.name: lat
fields.description: Latitude of the stop (WGS 84)

fields.name: locationType
fields.description: Identifies whether this stop represents a stop or station.

fields.name: lon
fields.description: Longitude of the stop (WGS 84)

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name of the stop, e.g. Pasilan asema

fields.name: parentStation
fields.description: The station which this stop is part of (or null if this stop is not part of a station)

fields.name: patterns
fields.description: Patterns which pass through this stop

fields.name: platformCode
fields.description: Identifier of the platform, usually a number. This value is only present for stops that are part of a station

fields.name: routes
fields.description: Routes which pass through this stop

fields.name: stopTimesForPattern
fields.description: Returns timetable of the specified pattern at this stop

fields.name: stops
fields.description: Returns all stops that are children of this station (Only applicable for stations)

fields.name: stoptimesForPatterns
fields.description: Returns list of stoptimes (arrivals and departures) at this stop, grouped by patterns

fields.name: stoptimesForServiceDate
fields.description: Returns list of stoptimes for the specified date

fields.name: stoptimesWithoutPatterns
fields.description: Returns list of stoptimes (arrivals and departures) at this stop

fields.name: transfers
fields.description: List of nearby stops which can be used for transfers

fields.name: vehicleMode
fields.description:
Transport mode (e.g. `BUS`) used by routes which pass through this stop or
`null` if mode cannot be determined, e.g. in case no routes pass through the stop.
Note that also other types of vehicles may use the stop, e.g. tram replacement
buses might use stops which have `TRAM` as their mode.

fields.name: wheelchairBoarding
fields.description: Whether wheelchair boarding is possible for at least some of vehicles on this stop

fields.name: zoneId
fields.description: ID of the zone where this stop is located

LegTime.name: LegTime
LegTime.description:
Time information about a passenger at a certain place. May contain real-time information if
available.

fields.name: estimated
fields.description: The estimated time of the event. If no real-time information is available, this is null.

fields.name: scheduledTime
fields.description: The scheduled time of the event.

RealTimeEstimate.name: RealTimeEstimate
RealTimeEstimate.description: Real-time estimates for a vehicle at a certain place.

fields.name: delay
fields.description:
The delay or "earliness" of the vehicle at a certain place.
  
If the vehicle is early then this is a negative duration.
